parts.note: the Red Devils are the Parachute Regiment's display team, so their men are paras
a camp is a site where people are based

explanation.surface: Someone hanging about the base of the army's famous parachute display team.
explanation.walkthrough: PARA is a member of the British Parachute Regiment, whose display team is called the Red Devils; 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off others, the very picture of a sponging hanger-on.

parts.note: a section is a part
leased means let

explanation.surface: A portion rented out by a marvellous lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means 'of fable': Dame Partlet is the hen in the fable of Chanticleer, in Chaucer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hen in the fable of the cock and the fox bears this name, so she is a dame of fable.

clue.text: Violent 'behaviour crooked stunt no longer new

parts.note: a ramp is a swindle, a dishonest trick
something ageing is growing old

explanation.surface: Wild conduct from a twisted trick that has gone stale.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMP is British slang for a swindle or racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing about in a wild frenzy is violent conduct.

clue.text: It's strap-hanging that suits the schoolboy's book

definitions.text: It's strap-hanging that suits the schoolboy's book

parts.words: It's strap-hanging that suits the schoolboy's book
parts.note: a school bag hangs from a strap and holds the pupil's books, suiting him in both senses

explanation.walkthrough: 'strap-hanging' suggests a commuter standing on a train; here it is a bag on a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag hangs by a strap over the shoulder and carries the pupil's books.

indicators.note: to change the letters is to give them a new order

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: The leading man of a Victorian prime minister's novel cannot alter his hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges CANT into TANC. Benjamin Disraeli, Victorian prime minister, also wrote novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli's 1847 novel is named after its hero, a young nobleman on a religious quest.

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's favourite old city
the chin is one of the facial features

explanation.surface: A hedgehog described as one of the sights of some historic town.
explanation.definitionFit: Urchin is an old country name for the spiny little mammal, which gave the sea urchin its name.

explanation.surface: A slack way of describing certain credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not fastened is loose, and credit given without collateral is described the same way.

clue.text: Weep about the lute destroyed with knives

indicators.note: one word goes round the other

parts.note: to weep is to cry

indicators.note: a thing destroyed is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crying over a musical instrument smashed with blades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges LUTE into UTLE, and 'about' puts CRY round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Knives, forks and spoons together make up the table implements.

clue.text: At a dead end, old star faces the facts

explanation.surface: Stuck, a faded celebrity accepts reality.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is what a fading star admits: 'I'm passé', past it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock with no way forward is a dead end, and an old star admitting 'I'm passé' (out of date) says the same letters.

clue.text: Faraway quality of the north-east in wild Somerset.

indicators.note: the compass letters sit inside the rearranged county name
wild letters run free, so the county's name is rearranged

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A remote air shared by England's far corner and the untamed West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges SOMERSET into REMOTESS, and 'in' puts NE into it. Somerset is a rural county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Remoteness is the state of lying far off, a distant or far-flung character.

explanation.surface: Something that strains out confidential intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette ends with filters are called filter tips, and tips are also inside hints passed on quietly, such as racing tips.

explanation.surface: Bikers' clothing that has got rather dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grubby' is read as 'being grubs': the larvae of the crane fly are known by this name, as are the hide coats bikers wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Crane-fly grubs share this name with hide coats worn by bikers, so it fits both readings.

clue.text: Attempted to get about £2— with bird imitations ?

definitions.note: describes singing done in the way a songbird warbles

indicators.note: to get about something is to go round it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: attempted means tried
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, so two pounds is two Ls

explanation.surface: Someone tries to earn a couple of pounds by doing birdsong impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get about' puts LL, two of the £ signs (L for libra, the pound), inside TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilling is the rapid warbling of songbirds, so a voice that has warbled has sung like a bird.

clue.text: River crustacean the French find abominable.

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a crab is a crustacean
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people find a crab from the river horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe flows through Exeter in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something execrable is utterly detestable, dreadful and loathsome.

clue.text: Old bird with some kind of grouse

parts.note: grey hair goes with age, so grey stands for old
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: An aged bird with a particular complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like a grumble; it is the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for the female black grouse, a species of game bird.

parts.note: a blacksmith forges the iron plate nailed to a horse's hoof

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smith' looks like a name, maybe a forger; it is a blacksmith.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron plate on a horse's hoof is made by a blacksmith at his forge.

parts.note: someone who wrangles is deep into a bargain, arguing over the price

explanation.definitionFit: One who argues over prices is a wrangler absorbed in striking a bargain.

clue.text: To.' fix Welsh prefix, has point

parts.note: ap, meaning son of, begins many Welsh surnames

explanation.surface: Correcting a Welsh name's opening has some purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: AP means 'son of' in Welsh names, as in ap Rhys, now Price.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to fix or settle a time or place.

parts.note: to gall is to annoy
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A ladies' man may irritate an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is a man who is attentive and courteous to women.

clue.text: Red maid is uncommonly highly thought of

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A red-haired servant girl is unusually well regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' rearranges REDMAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something admired is regarded with approval and respect.

indicators.note: something duplicated appears twice over, so the short name is written two times

parts.note: Alf is short for Alfred
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Alfred makes a double copy of a piece about a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucerne' looks like the Swiss city; it is the fodder plant, known in Britain by that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is the British name for the fodder crop grown for hay.

clue.text: Has importance for makers of: floor coverings.?

explanation.surface: Rug weavers carry some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as mat-ters, those who make mats.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that counts is significant, and people who make mats would be mat-ters.

explanation.surface: Rodents and where they fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' is a verb: to rat is to abandon a cause. The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is to abandon, and the Desert Rats fought in sandy wastes in the Second World War.

parts.note: their ship was named after a flower, the May blossom, and carried settlers to a fresh start

explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' is a ship, not a skill; 'blooming' points to the flower in the ship's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1620 English settlers sailed to America on the Mayflower, a vessel named after a blossom.

parts.note: Mount Ida is a mountain of Greek myth, in Crete and in Asia Minor

explanation.surface: An opera set on a mountain of the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's work set in ancient Egypt is one of the best-known operas.

explanation.surface: Followers flocking behind the leader of a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' also reads as a leader with a ring: the lead sheep wears a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The bell-wearing ram leads the flock, so the sheep follow it, and by extension it is any leader of a movement.

clue.text: Figure that may be cut by the maker

definitions.text: Figure that may be cut by the maker

parts.words: Figure that may be cut by the maker
parts.note: a sculptor carves a likeness out of stone, so its maker cuts this figure

explanation.definitionFit: A carved likeness in stone is a figure chiselled by the sculptor who makes it.

clue.text: Stop women being 'heard : they sound ominous.

parts.note: to ban is to stop

indicators.note: the plural of a female pronoun is said aloud, giving spelling by sound

parts.note: women are shes, the plural of the pronoun she

explanation.surface: Forbid the ladies from being audible, for their voices are menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEES is heard as 'shes', women. A banshee is the Irish spirit whose wail foretells a death.
explanation.definitionFit: These Irish spirits wail to foretell a death, so their cries are a dire warning.
